title: Security QnA field handoff — customer playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for handling customer security questionnaires (QnA) where the ask touches RBAC v2, audit log schema, SIEM exports, and evidence automation. The doc is intentionally pragmatic — a field-friendly script + handoff checklist for solutions engineering / security to give to customers or to stitch together an evidence package quickly.

Audience:
- Solutions engineering / customer security engineers
- Sales engineers responding to security questionnaires
- Internal security reviewers who curate evidence bundles

High-level approach (one-pager script):
1) Intake: capture the questionnaire scope and required evidence types (policies, screenshots, log samples, retention certs). Note any deadlines.
2) Map asks to artifacts: RBAC questions -> role matrix + change history; Audit log questions -> sample events and schema; SIEM export questions -> export fields + sample JSON/NDJSON; Evidence automation questions -> whether we can produce bulk evidence via the evidence-export API.
3) Triage: decide what is ready (final) vs what is "work-in-progress" (WIP) and flag to customer.
4) Deliver: assemble a zip with labeled artifacts and a cover note that maps each artifact to questionnaire IDs.

Quick answers and scripts you can paste into QnA responses:
- "RBAC model": "We implement a role-based model (RBAC v2) with bounded roles (system, admin, operator, viewer) and attribute-based access controls for certain endpoints. Role assignments and changes are recorded in the audit log and retained for 365 days by default; retention can be extended under enterprise contracts."
- "Audit logs": "All control-plane activities (role changes, API key events, deployment rollouts, console logins) are captured in structured JSON audit logs, delivered to our internal telemetry pipeline and optionally exported to customer SIEMs via secure delivery (S3/HTTPS). We provide a schema and sample records on request."
- "SIEM export": "We support NDJSON export and a customer-specific field mapping layer. Exports are pushed to customer S3 buckets with server-side encryption, or available via pull-based signed-URL packages for ad-hoc requests."

Artifact mapping (how to map questionnaire sections to deliverables):
- RBAC policy & evidence: role-list CSV, role-to-permission matrix (CSV), sample role change event (audit log JSON), admin review SOP (doc).
- Access provisioning: onboarding runbook, JIT provisioning notes, recent provisioning audit (last 90 days).
- Audit log schema: schema doc (JSON schema), sample events (NDJSON), retention policy statement, ingestion pipeline diagram (png).
- SIEM export: field mapping table, example NDJSON export, delivery SLA and encryption notes, customer-config instructions (S3 path + IAM template).
- Evidence automation: API spec for evidence-bundle generation, sample CLI commands, rate limits and expected runtime for typical bundles.

Sample audit log event (copyable):
{"timestamp":"2026-01-22T14:03:11Z","tenant_id":"acct_0x123","actor_id":"user_UA78","actor_role":"admin","action":"role.update","resource":"role:dedicated-gpu-admin","outcome":"success","request_id":"req_9f2a","meta":{"ip":"34.91.12.8","user_agent":"Console/1.2.3"}}

SIEM export field mapping (short):
- timestamp -> event_time (ISO8601)
- tenant_id -> customer_id
- actor_id -> principal_id
- actor_role -> role
- action -> event_type
- resource -> resource_id
- outcome -> status
- request_id -> trace_id
- meta.ip -> src_ip

Evidence automation play (practical):
- Use: evidence-bundles API (POST /v1/evidence/bundles) with query parameters: tenant_id, time_range, artifact_types=[audit_logs,role_bindings,config_snapshots].
- Output: signed URL to NDJSON + CSV manifest.
- Ops notes: typical generation for 30 days of audit logs for medium tenant (100k events) takes ~6-10 minutes; we throttle concurrent exports at 4 per-org to protect pipeline.
- Security: export URLs are single-use, expire in 24h by default; enterprise options for customer-side S3 delivery exist.

Common customer Qs (field answers / follow-ups):
Q: "Can you provide role change history for the last 12 months?"
A: Yes — we can produce NDJSON for role.change events. Ask the customer to confirm timeframe and delivery method (S3 vs signed package). If they need >365 days retention, escalate to CSM for contract addendum.

Q: "Does the audit log include request/response payloads?"
A: Control-plane logs record metadata and request parameters but exclude full response payloads and PII by default. If a customer needs additional payload capture, this requires a scoped change and privacy review.

Q: "How do we integrate logs into our SIEM?"
A: Provide them the field mapping table, the recommended ingest template (S3 layout + sample IAM role), and an example NDJSON bundle. For Splunk/QRadar, include the sample ingestion JSON configuration (we maintain templates in the Confluence linked above).

Handoff checklist (deliverables & ownership):
- [ ] Role matrix CSV (owner: product-security)
- [ ] RBAC change audit NDJSON (owner: infra-telemetry)
- [ ] Schema doc + README (owner: product-security)
- [ ] Evidence automation CLI sample (owner: devops)
- [ ] SIEM field-mapping sheet (owner: integrations)
- [ ] Signed delivery package or S3 access (owner: solutions-eng)

Notes / things to surface to security reviewers:
- Any ask for retention > 365 days or for raw request payloads must be routed to Compliance + Legal.
- Exports containing user identifiers may need a Data Processing Amendment for certain customers (list countries/regimes).
- If customer requests push integration to a customer-managed SIEM via streaming, validate network topology and cross-account IAM policies with infra team.

Open questions / TODOs (WIP):
- Confirm default retention values in RBAC v2 design doc (confluence) — are we 365 or 400 days? TODO: Maya to confirm with telemetry team (ENG-1284).
- Build a pre-made evidence bundle template for "SOC 2 initial review" use case. (Priority: medium)
- Add sample Splunk HEC ingest JSON to the template folder.

Last-mile delivery language (cover note template):
"Attached is the evidence bundle requested in your security questionnaire (Q: SECTION X). Files are labeled with the corresponding question IDs. If you need additional context or a walk-through of the sample events, we’re happy to schedule a session with our security engineer"
